learning_outcomes.text: Explain the basic principles and application areas of Markov chains.
Be able to model and analyze systems with Markov chains.
Be able to recognize the basic concepts and types of queuing theory.
Be able to analyze the performance criteria of queuing systems.
Be able to analyze queuing network models such as open and closed Jackson networks.
Be able to recognize, analyze and use network models in optimization problems.
Be able to understand deterministic and probabilistic inventory models and apply them to inventory management problems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Markov Chains, Network Models and Queuing Systems
Queueing networks: Opened and Closed Jackson network
Queueing networks: Opened and Closed Jackson network
assessment_rules: The final success grade is calculated by combining the Midterm Examination (Semester Learning Activities) with 40% contribution and the Final Examination (End of Semester Learning Activities) with 60% contribution.
